notes_markdown:
- **Albums no longer show every photo twice.** Uploading to an Immich
  album, or adding a photo with the album picker (`Shift+I`), used to put
  both the RAW and the JPEG in the album, and the Immich album view shows
  them as two separate photos. culler now adds the JPEG only; the RAW
  stays behind it in the stack, so developing from an album still works.
  Albums filled earlier keep their doubles — toggle a photo out and back
  in with `Shift+I` to fix it, or remove the RAWs in Immich.

- **Photos from an Immich server show the time they were taken.** Their
  capture time used to read in UTC, so in Amsterdam a photo taken at 08:37
  showed 07:37, and an evening shot could sort under the next day. culler
  now uses the camera's own local time, the same one the Immich timeline
  shows.
- **Every filter shows its size.** The rail's Filter palette counts each
  filter before you pick it. Empty filters are greyed out but still
  clickable, and a row of ≥1★ … ≥5★ chips appears once anything is
  rated. `F`, `Cmd+1`–`5`, `Shift+Y` and `Shift+U` name the filter and
  its count on the status line (`Filter: Picks · 312`), as does the ⋯
  menu's Filter row. An empty filter says which one it is and how to
  move on. The bottom-right counters gain a hollow ring counting the
  photos still **undecided** (no pick or reject yet), so the work left
  in a cull is always in view. On a partly loaded large Immich library
  the counts carry a `+`.
- **Moments are found for you.** Photos of the same situation — from
  one camera, each taken within 4 s of the previous one by default (read
  from the capture time, to the millisecond where the camera records
  it) — now group into moments, whether that's a burst of fast frames
  or a slower run of the same scene: a thin bracket under their
  thumbnails in the filmstrip, a `[moment 3/8]` tag on the photo, and
  `,` / `.` to jump to the previous / next moment in the normal view,
  the Grid and Survey. `N` on a moment now surveys exactly that moment
  (the 24 around you in a longer one) instead of whatever happened to
  sit nearby. Moments follow the filter, so under Unrated the ones
  you've judged simply drop out of the way. Change the gap in Settings
  (`Cmd+,`) — 0.5 s groups only strict bursts.
- **Settings (`Cmd+,`).** A small sheet over the photo — from the
  culler menu, the ⋯ menu or `Cmd+,` — gathers the things you might want
  to change: the moment gap (the filmstrip regroups behind the sheet as
  you drag it, and two lines count your moments and name the one you're
  on), auto-advance, how fast every slider moves when you drag it (Fine,
  Standard or Direct), the JPEG quality `J` and exports use (the same
  value as the Batch panel's Quality card, whose slider now also moves
  cleanly one step at a time on a slow drag), how much disk the preview
  cache may use (with how much it holds now, and buttons to show or clear
  it), whether culler checks for updates at launch, **Show tips again**
  for the one-time hints, and **Show log file**, which shows culler's
  diagnostic log in Finder for a problem report. Every change applies at
  once and is remembered; the keyboard drives it too (`↑`/`↓`, `←`/`→`,
  `Tab`, `R` resets, `Esc` closes). Auto-advance (`T`) is now remembered
  across launches.
- **`Enter` in Survey keeps one.** It picks the focused photo and
  rejects every other photo in the grid you haven't flagged or rated
  yet — earlier picks and rated photos are never touched — and with
  auto-advance on, deals the next moment.
- **Sort photos into folders with the number keys.** Pin up to nine
  folders under **Sort destinations** in the apply panel (`A`, with Copy
  or Move chosen), each set to move or copy, then press `Shift+D` for
  sort mode: `1`–`9` send the photo — or your selection — to that folder,
  RAW, JPEG and sidecar together, with a receipt on the status line. A
  blue **[sort]** tag and a rail of your folders show the mode is on;
  `Shift+D`, `Esc` or the rail's **Done** leaves it. The first move into
  each folder asks for a second press, a same-named file already there
  leaves your photo in place, and an unplugged drive is refused instead
  of recreated. The batch **Move** and **Copy** also got stricter: a
  photo whose JPEG or sidecar name is already taken in the destination
  is now left entirely in place, where before its RAW could go ahead
  alone.
- **Pivot to the same day, camera, lens or moment — and come straight
  back.** `Shift+G` (or a click on the info panel's Captured, Moment,
  Camera or Lens row, which now show how many photos share them) narrows
  the view to every photo that shares that detail with the one you're
  on, with a strip above the photo saying where you are. Judge, filter
  and select inside as usual; `Esc` returns to the exact photo, filter
  and grid scroll you left, and `Enter` leaves the pivot but stays on
  the photo you're looking at. The batch panel offers **This view (N)**
  while you're in one.
- **Group the grid by day or by moment.** `G` in the grid (`K`) puts
  each capture day — or each moment, with the single photos between them
  gathered into one quiet group — under its own header, and `G` again
  moves on to the next grouping and back to the plain grid. Each header
  counts its picks, rejects and undecided photos as you go, has a box
  that selects (or deselects) the whole group, jumps to the group's
  first photo when you click its title, and on a moment offers a
  **Survey** button that opens that moment straight away. The arrow keys
  step over the headers row by row.
- **Save every unsaved server edit in one go.** The apply panel (`A`) on
  an Immich source gains **Save edits to server** — the batch form of
  `J`: every photo in the scope that still needs saving is rendered,
  uploaded as its stack cover and has its grade saved, one after the
  other, with "Saving · 4 of 12" and the current photo's phase in the
  panel and the pill, and Cancel stopping cleanly between photos. An
  **Unsaved** scope (this action only) targets exactly the photos behind
  the corner count; a selection works too. Photos culler couldn't load a
  grade or crop for are skipped and named — never re-rendered plain over
  an existing edit — and on a large library the summary says how many
  unsaved photos sit outside the loaded part. Failures name the photos
  and the primary button becomes "Retry N failed…".
- **Unsaved server edits now have a place on every screen.** A blue
  "12 unsaved" chip in the bottom-right corner totals the develop, crop
  and landmark edits you haven't saved with `J`, across every Immich
  source you've added; click it (or press `Shift+U`) to see just those
  photos on the open server — each drops out of the view the moment it
  saves — and rest the pointer on it for the per-server breakdown, where
  a click opens that server straight onto its unsaved photos. The number
  is exact within seconds of opening a server: culler now checks every
  edited photo it hadn't proven saved against the server in the
  background, one request at a time, so a photo whose saved grade
  already matches stops counting and one deleted on the server is
  forgotten — including photos outside the loaded window of a large
  library. `Shift+U` is also in the Filter menu and the ⋯ popover.
- **The diagnostic log now narrates every batch.** Copy, move, trash,
  export, download, archive and upload from the apply panel each write
  what was dispatched (action, scope, photo count, destination), one
  line per photo with its outcome or the reason it failed, a line when
  you cancel, and a closing count with the elapsed time — so a batch
  from last week can be reconstructed from `~/.culler/logs/culler.log`
  instead of from memory.
- **The sources pane counts your unsaved server edits.** Each Immich
  source's row now says "12 unsaved" — the photos whose develop, crop or
  landmark alignment hasn't been saved with `J` yet, for every server
  you've added, not only the open one. Ratings and picks sync on their
  own and never count; folders never show it. culler now also records
  which edits it has proven saved, so the count survives a restart, and
  a `J` no longer leaves a stale copy of the photo's state behind under
  its old name. The first launch after this version may read high until
  the photos are opened. A landmark-only change (an alignment without a
  crop or grade) finally shows as unsaved too.
- **Quitting with unsaved server edits now reminds you once.** Close
  culler while develop grades or crops on an Immich source haven't been
  saved with `J`, and the first Quit is held back with a count on the
  status line; press Quit again to leave them for later — they stay in
  culler's own state file, nothing is lost — or save first.
- **Inside a stack, culler's own render row no longer applies its crop
  and grade a second time.** Stepping into a server stack with `G` and
  looking at the re-rendered cover showed the crop over an already
  cropped picture, and `J` from that row cropped the render itself
  again. The row now knows it is culler's render and renders from the
  stack's RAW, exactly like the cover outside the stack.
- **Landmark align no longer doubles a server photo's previous crop.**
  Aligning a photo that culler had already re-rendered once, with its
  RAW showing in the pane, stored the old crop applied twice — the
  frame drifted away from the reference the moment you accepted. The
  solve now knows whether it was made on the RAW or on the rendered
  JPEG and stores the crop once either way. If a series you aligned
  today looks off, re-enter the pass on that photo and press `Enter`
  again; the stored points are fine.
- **The upload speed graph holds still and says what it means.** Its
  bars used to re-slice a sliding window every frame and rescale to
  whatever peak happened to be in view, so they wobbled constantly
  without meaning anything. Each bar is now a fixed five seconds of the
  batch that never changes once complete, the row steps left one bar at
  a time, the lighter rightmost bar is the five seconds in progress
  drawn at its current speed, and a caption ("up to 20 MB/s") says what
  a full-height bar means — a scale that only steps up during a batch.
  The speed next to "MB left" now stays put between files instead of
  blinking out.
- **The info panel says "no value" one way, everywhere.** Camera, lens,
  place, description, people and album rows that have nothing to show
  now render nothing at all — never a stray dash. A description with
  nothing typed reads "Add a description" (a click-to-edit invitation,
  the one field that has to stay visible), and a people/albums fetch
  that fails now reads "Couldn't load people & albums" — leaving that
  photo and coming back genuinely retries it, instead of staying stuck
  for the rest of the session.
- **Landmarks are saved with the photos, and the walk starts on the
  reference.** `Shift+C` now works on the reference's own crop pass:
  place its points once, then `Enter` walks the series with those dots
  already on every photo. `M` saves the points alongside the crops (in
  the sidecar, or with the server copy), so adding a photo to an
  aligned series later means opening Match Look, pressing `Enter`, and
  clicking that one photo's points — already-aligned photos are skipped.
  A **Clear landmarks** button in the crop pane forgets the set, and
  `Esc`'s confirm now counts landmark edits too.
- **`J` on a server photo says what it is waiting on.** The pending-work
  pill used to read "Uploading" from the first moment, while a
  tens-of-megabytes RAW was still coming *down*. It now walks the real
  phases — "Downloading RAW · name" with the megabytes so far, the total
  and the speed on hover (amber when nothing moves for five seconds,
  like uploads), then "Rendering · name", then "Uploading · name" with
  the upload's own count. The diagnostic log records the same steps.
- **Rating and flagging server photos writes to disk less.** culler's
  local copy of a server library's edits used to be rewritten whole on
  every keystroke; it now settles a quarter of a second after the last
  change (and always on quit). The one trade: a hard crash inside that
  quarter second can lose the very last edit — a rating or flag is
  re-sent to the server on the next launch regardless.
- **Oversized server responses are refused, not swallowed.** A server
  answer far larger than any sane one (a runaway page, a corrupt saved
  grade) now fails that one step with a clear message instead of
  reading without limit into memory.
- **A sources pane you can read at a glance.** The pane (`S`) groups
  your sources under **Folders** and **Servers**, draws a small icon
  for each kind instead of a bracketed tag, and shows where each one
  lives — your home folder as `~`, long paths shortened from the front
  so the folder's own name survives. The always-green dot is gone: a
  row only carries a mark when something is wrong (amber = out of reach
  for now, red = needs you), with the reason spelled out beside it, and
  a scanning source shows a spinner and its progress. Adding is a
  compact **+ Add** beside the heading, an empty pane offers one **Add
  source** button, the keys for the row you're on sit at the pane's
  foot, renaming happens in a proper edit field, and a large server's
  **Load all** is always visible on its row. Pointing at a row
  highlights it without moving your selection. Opening an album now
  marks that album — not its server too — as the one you're in.
- **Every source shows its photo count, and says when it's in trouble.**
  The sources pane shows each source's photo count on the right — live
  for the one you have open, and from your last visit for the others
  (culler never reads a folder you don't have open just to count it, so
  macOS doesn't prompt you). A saved folder, card or share that's gone
  reads "Not found" or "Card not inserted"; a server that didn't answer
  last time reads "Can't reach …"; a server whose API key was refused —
  or whose key this copy of culler can no longer read from the
  keychain — says so in red, with the fix: add the server again. The
  pane also no longer checks every saved folder on disk while it's
  drawing; it checks once, in the background, each time it opens.
